doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Bass playing, avant-garde and the state of the music
title: Monk at Carnegie Hall and music for love
summary: Ware recalls Monk saying the music was too fast, and the sold-out Carnegie Hall concert with young white audience.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well, that was the whole thing. That's another thing I admire about Thelonius. He was saying something -- Patrick asked him, say, "Man, what do you think about the music? Monk said, 'It's so fast, it took the beauty out of music?' Actually, he doesn't want to play anymore.
You know? I was thankful that we were able to go up there and catch him at the Carnegie and that whole house was 90 percent packed with white college-age kids.
The hall was sold out. And he Thelonius was so beautiful, so beautiful. He hasn't played.
It just makes you wish, though, that you always want to see people with that kind of ability and the ideal circumstances --
-- and you never see them under ideal circumstances.

No, either they're in some little smoke-infested hall, you know, standing in the bathroom with no dressing room, nothing to cool out, or either standing outside, catching pneumonia. Oh, well, that's a sign of the times.
